channel.title: DevPulse · Research
channel.description: Daily research stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: LeWAM trains a world model and action policy end to end
item.description: LeWAM jointly trains latent-state prediction and action flow matching, improving success from 28.6% to 89.7% on contact-rich tasks and planning 32.3× faster. The results make an integrated latent-world-model approach worth examining for embodied control.

item.title: Frontier models struggle to reproduce human ML innovation
item.description: InnovationEval tests whether models can independently devise ML techniques comparable to human work; the excerpt says recent models made little progress despite thousands of dollars in GPU experiments. The evaluation targets a key gap in claims about automating AI research.

item.title: A trial finds AI-assisted work improves judgment for senior patent attorneys, not juniors
item.description: In a three-month randomized trial, senior attorneys who routinely used AI showed stronger judgment, while junior attorneys had no average skill gain and a wider spread of scores. The results raise practical questions about AI’s effects on learning and expertise at work.

item.title: OuroWorld animates static 3D Gaussian splats into looping scenes
item.description: OuroWorld combines generated reference video with a periodic deformation field and grounded drift field to create looping motion in 3D scenes; it reports winning 70.8%–99.0% of user-study comparisons across 39 scenes. The method may interest engineers working on 3D generation pipelines.

item.title: Longer context does not make LLMs reliably recover sequential rules
item.description: Controlled Rock–Paper–Scissors and n-gram experiments find that longer context does not improve strategy identification, recognition does not guarantee faithful simulation, and higher-order dependencies impair rule recovery. These results caution against treating behavioral imitation as evidence that a model learned the underlying process.

item.title: OpenAI’s mathematics results spur debate over mathematical progress
item.description: The excerpt points to 372 results released by OpenAI and describes reactions from mathematicians, including a reference to RL vs. L. Engineers tracking AI’s ability to contribute to research can use the discussion as a prompt to examine the underlying results.

item.title: Lean verifies an optimal packing of 11 squares with no admissions
item.description: The verification run accepted 7,920 Lean modules and reports zero admissions; selected exact numerical checks use native_decide, so the claim is not kernel-only. The proof and explicit trust boundary make this a concrete reference for formal verification workflows.

item.title: Lean verification cannot guarantee an AI-generated natural-language proof is sound
item.description: The paper argues that mechanically checking a Lean formalization does not establish that it faithfully represents the original natural-language proof. Engineers building AI verification workflows should treat translation fidelity as a separate problem from checking the formal result.

item.title: Bidirectional type slicing finds minimal code explanations for type information
item.description: The paper formalizes slices that explain synthesized or expected types, proves every query has a minimal slice, and shows that refining a query monotonically shrinks it. The exact and approximate methods could inform better explanations in programming tools.

item.title: New algorithms give polynomial speedups for 3SUM and APSP
item.description: The paper reports deterministic runtimes of O(n^1.9992) for 3SUM and O(n^2.9995) for APSP, refuting their standard complexity hypotheses. It is a notable theoretical result, though the excerpt does not establish practical gains on real workloads.

item.title: Tail-Influence Sampling allocates rollouts to improve CVaR estimates
item.description: Tail-Influence Sampling estimates which conditional components most affect policy CVaR, then reallocates evaluation queries; on CliffWalking it reduces MSE by 41% versus learned occupancy and 76% versus a comparison method. The method offers a principled way to spend limited rollout budgets on rare failures.

item.title: ScholarCatalyst finds agentic search trails embedding retrieval on expert judgments
item.description: The benchmark uses judgments from 184 lead authors across 207 papers; agentic search reaches 0.42 Recall@20 versus 0.48 for embedding retrieval, while a stronger agent reaches 0.51. It gives engineers a grounded test of whether research agents add value over retrieval tools.
